speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) to date, what is the number of children in Singapore diagnosed with COVID-19 and what proportion has the Delta variant; (b) how many needed supplementary oxygen at any time during their illness; and (c) how does this experience compare with countries with significant numbers of COVID-19 Delta variant infections in children.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) how can the safety of children be ensured before a suitable COVID-19 vaccine for them is available, especially children who are immunocompromised; (b) whether the Ministry is monitoring the trend of long COVID-19 symptoms in children; and (c) whether adequate resources are available to provide healthcare and emotional support for children who contract long COVID.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Global data show that a very low proportion of COVID-19 infected children experience a severe illness, as compared to adults.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The percentage of infected children who experience severe illness and require intensive care is 0.7% in Israel, 0.3% in the Republic of Korea and 0.6% in France.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is evidence suggesting that children with underlying medical conditions, such as genetic, neurologic, metabolic conditions, medical complexity, congenital heart disease, obesity, diabetes, asthma, chronic lung disease, sickle cell disease, or immunosuppression might be at increased risk for severe illness from COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are, however, mindful that the number of cases in the community is rising and there may be more children infected with COVID-19 in the future.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will ensure that these children receive appropriate care, if their illness is more severe.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are things parents can do to minimise the risk of their children getting infected or developing severe illnesses.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: All family members should maintain good hygiene and keep their home clean.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: When out, keep your masks on and cut back on social activities where masks are off or the interactions are prolonged, because such interactions account for the large majority of infections.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: When unwell, do a self-test or see a doctor immediately.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These effective safe management and surveillance have been implemented to further keep our children safe, particularly in large settings where children congregate, such as preschools and schools.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These include mask-wearing, limiting the group size, personal hygiene and requiring those children with a higher risk to take leave of absence.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Family members should also get vaccinated to reduce the risks of being infected and transmitting COVID-19 to the child.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Immunocompromised children are at risk from COVID-19 and other infectious diseases.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They and their family should exercise additional precautions, such as avoiding crowded places and minimising the number of visitors.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As for "long COVID", it is an informal term that refers to persons who have continued symptoms of COVID-19 infection.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The underlying reasons for continued symptoms vary, as do the symptoms themselves.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Locally, infected children have, generally, not had prolonged symptoms.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will offer care to all patients with long COVID, if this occurs, and especially those that require support from different clinical teams, depending on their conditions.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some parents have been watching what has happened overseas in some other countries: long COVID as well as the Multi-system Inflammatory Syndrome in children reported in some countries where COVID-19 is widespread; some parents also look at what happens in some advanced economies —

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: First, can the Minister share whether there have been any cases of Multi-system Inflammatory Syndrome documented so far in Singapore among our paediatric COVID-19 patients?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, can the Senior Minister of State also share, given the different experience on both sides of the Atlantic, what lessons can we learn from studying other countries' battles with COVID-19 to safeguard and support our children?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The short answer to the first question is no.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are no paediatric cases, such as what he has described.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As for the different experience overseas, indeed, the lessons learnt are something that our various expert committees and professionals in various disciplines are looking at very, very closely.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are a lot of lessons to be learnt but if I could summarise a few things.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, when we take these lessons from overseas, how they are applied here will depend, for example, on the baseline health of our population, whether it is child or adult; on access to care, and we are very fortunate that within the confines of our city, tertiary medical care is a very short distance away; on the general level of hygiene; and also, on the ability for our population to comply with various procedures or requirements, whether medical or social.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, context is everything and the baseline health of our population is also very, very important.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We cannot just simply take the raw numbers or the raw experience from overseas and expect that exactly the same thing will happen here in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I think when the decisions are reached, we will certainly be quite clear and make full explanation to the public.
